correctness.rationale: On a chain the Fang–Fourier–Litza–Pegel transfer is globally linear and invertible: y1=x1, yi=xi−t xi−1, xi=∑_{k=1}^i t^(i−k)yk. The m+1 nonnegative order-simplex slacks s0=x1, sj=xj+1−xj, sm=1−xm telescope to 1, and their gradients in y have the specified norms N0=1, Nj=sqrt(1+(1−t)^2 ∑_(ℓ=0)^(j−1)t^(2ℓ)), Nm=sqrt(∑_(ℓ=0)^(m−1)t^(2ℓ)). The distances to facets are sj/Nj; the Chebyshev center is uniquely obtained by equalizing all m+1 distances, giving r=1/∑Nj and cumulative-slack coordinates. Direct endpoint substitution and differentiation give D′(0)=−(m−1)/sqrt2 and D′(1)=(m−1)sqrt m/2, guaranteeing a strictly better interior radius for every m≥2. At m=2 strict convexity and symmetry force t=1/2 with r=1/(1+sqrt5). All-dimensional proof symbolic; SymPy corroborated endpoint gradients for m=2,3,4,7.
